transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I guess I'm here because... well, I hope it's okay that I came in for this, I really don't want to waste your time. But I've just been having this feeling lately that I've completely let my family down. We took on this mortgage, and... I don't know, I just feel terrible about it. 

And at work—I wait tables—every time I make even a small mistake, it just feels like it proves that I'm... well, that I'm just useless. Like I deserve whatever bad things happen to me. I know that probably sounds a bit dramatic, I'm sorry. Does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing I should be coming in for?
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or hopeless most of the day?

Um, yeah, I guess I have been. I really try not to let it show, especially at the restaurant, because I want to be a good employee. But most days... there’s just this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. 

I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? Carrying plates to tables and smiling because I’m supposed to, not because I actually feel anything good inside. I hope that doesn't make me sound ungrateful for my job, I really do try to stay positive. Is that... does that answer your question okay?
About how long have you been feeling this way?

Well, I guess if I really think about it... the heavy, sad feelings, and just feeling so guilty about everything... it's been going on for a while. Maybe about a year and two months? Give or take a little bit. 

I mean, it's not like I'm crying all day every single day or anything. I still go to work, I still try my best to be helpful. I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining or wallowing in it. But yeah, those periods where I just feel so down and guilty... they've been around for about that long. Does that sound like what you were asking? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Before this started about a year ago, had you ever gone through a period where you felt this depressed?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I've had days where I felt a little down, like anyone else, I guess, but nothing like this. Before last year, I was usually pretty okay. I always tried to keep a good attitude, especially for work and for my family. 

I don't think I ever felt this... this stuck before. I hope that's the right answer. I'm trying to remember as best I can, but I really don't think I've ever felt this bad in the past. Is that helpful?
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy doing?

Um, I guess maybe a little bit? I really try to stay engaged with people, I promise I do. But... well, I used to really like joking around with the regulars at the restaurant, and I'd always text my brother right after my shifts just to chat and catch up. 

Lately, though, I kind of just... I mostly keep my face straight at work and only say what I absolutely have to say to get the orders right. And with my brother's texts, I just let the messages sit there on my phone. I just don't feel that pull to answer them anymore. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible brother, or like I'm being rude to the customers. I really don't mean to be, and I still make sure I'm polite! It's just hard to find that spark right now. Is that... is that the kind of thing you meant?
How has your sleep been during this past year or so?

Um, my sleep? It's... it's been okay, I think. I mean, I definitely still get some sleep, so it's not like I'm up all night causing problems or anything. 

I guess maybe I've been a little tired sometimes, but I really try not to let it affect my shifts at the restaurant. I know how important it is to be alert for the customers. I might toss and turn just a tiny bit, but I promise I'm still getting enough rest to do my job properly. I don't want you to think I'm neglecting my health or anything like that. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering that right.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over this past year?

Um, my appetite? It's... well, it's been a little bit unpredictable, I guess. I really try to make sure I eat enough to keep my energy up for work, I promise I do. 

But... well, my eating has been kind of all over the place lately. Some weeks, I'll barely even touch the staff meal during my shift. I just don't feel like it. And then other nights, I'll come home and just eat whatever's in the kitchen, just trying to feel... I don't know, settled, I guess? 

I haven't gained or lost a ton of weight or anything crazy, though! My uniform still fits fine, so it hasn't been a huge problem. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm completely out of control with my eating. I'm really trying to do better with it. Is that okay? Did I explain that right?
Have you had any thoughts that you would be better off dead, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

Oh, no, I... I definitely don't have any kind of plan to hurt myself. I would never actually do that, I promise. I know how terrible that would be. 

But, um... well, I guess sometimes, like when I'm lying awake in bed before an early shift, I... I do sometimes have this thought that it might just be easier if I didn't wake up. Just so I wouldn't have to keep feeling like I'm failing at everything right now. 

I really hope that doesn't sound too alarming, or make you think I'm a danger to myself. I swear I'm not going to do anything bad, it's really just a passing thought when I'm overwhelmed. I try to push it right out of my head. Is it okay that I told you that? I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient and giving you the right information.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt unusually energized, euphoric, or wired, where you needed very little sleep and felt like your thoughts were racing?

Oh, no, definitely not. I've never felt anything like that. I mean, sometimes I have a good day where I feel a little more awake or get through my shift without feeling so dragged down, but never wired or racing or anything extreme. 

I always try to stay pretty grounded, you know? I wouldn't want to be acting strange or hyper around the customers or my coworkers. I just try to keep my head down and do my job. So, no, I've never had a time where I didn't need sleep or felt euphoric like that. I hope that's the right answer... I just want to be honest with you. Does that make sense?
